history.text: Tell me about your debates with Douglas.

In the summer and autumn of 1858, Judge Douglas and I met seven times across Illinois, before crowds of thousands. The question was slavery in the territories: he held that each territory should decide for itself, and I held that a house divided against itself cannot stand. I lost the Senate seat, but the country was listening.

history.text: How did your flight in the 14-bis go?

On the 23rd of October 1906, at Bagatelle, the 14-bis rose from the grass under its own power and flew some sixty metres before the eyes of the Aéro-Club. In November I flew two hundred and twenty metres, and Paris cheered as if the sky had opened.
